title: USACE focuses on safety during Hurricane Ian recovery efforts
description: UASCE Hurricane Ian safety manager and St. Louis District employee discusses the steps that USACE is taking to ensure responders are safey during the recovery  efforts.
keywords: FEMA, jacksonville district, Ian, Hurricane Ian, HurricaneIan22, USACE
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District

transcript.text: Hi , I'm Sarah Futrell . I am the chief
of safety and occupational health with
the ST louis district . I am currently
deployed in Southwest florida for the
Hurricane Ian recovery efforts . The
importance of safety is to ensure that
our employees are able to provide
support to the people of Southwest
florida and they are able to assist in
the recovery efforts . We want to make
sure that they aren't getting sick ,
that they understand the hazards that
are there going to be confronted with
and that they're able to go home to
their families . So some of the things
that we're focused on to ensure the
safety of our employees is to identify
the different hazards that are within
the workplace or within the recovery
efforts like the blue roof mission and
people are doing , they're doing the
infrastructure assessments and walking
around houses that have debris
everywhere and they have to be on their
toes about what uh , where they're
walking and what they're doing . And
then there's also structural engineers
that are going into homes that are
assessing the damage to the houses and
it can be very dangerous . And so we
want to make sure that we are providing
them with the tools to do their job
safely . We're working 12 hours a day ,
seven days a week with long hour days .
It really puts a drain on our employees .
And so that's where we want to make
sure that they have the proper rest
there drinking plenty of water ,
they're protecting themselves from the
sun and so they can continue doing the
great work that we do And there's a lot
of driving time driving is really one
of our biggest hazards that we have
here . In addition to the driving
concerns , there is debris everywhere .
We have people that are technical
monitors for the debris mission , for
supporting fema and the state , in that
there's a lot of drywall and mold . So
we brought in an occupational health
nurse also to assist us with projecting
and protecting employees from exposures .
So we want to make sure that we're
providing our employees with the proper
tools to be able to protect themselves
against that . Because at the end of
the day , what we're here to do is to
make sure that our employees are able
to provide support that's needed , but
also able to do it safely and are able
to go home to their families .
Mhm .
